data.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar has hard-won structured-output behavior split between bespoke retry orchestration and Pydantic AI. The approved RP-01 plan makes Pydantic AI authoritative for Agent turns, structured-output retries, fallback, usage limits, and instrumentation while retaining Rebar policy for deterministic repair, provider safety, failure taxonomy, provenance, and artifacts. Recovery authority and the complete approved behavior ledger are recorded on `sandstone-fiendish-auk` and `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-research.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Structured-output validation and recovery execute through one Pydantic Agent operation with the approved shared request budget; verified by the child retry-contract tests covering tool turns, output retries, and exhaustion.
- [ ] Retry context never truncates authoritative input, accepted output, or stored history; the complete failed response is included only on proven fit and otherwise omitted whole, verified by the child complete/omit and oversize-input tests.
- [ ] Rebar preserves deterministic extraction, fallback eligibility, terminal refusal/filter behavior, typed exhaustion, final-failure artifacts, and answering-model provenance; verified by the mapped child regression matrices.
- [ ] Successful operations report complete Pydantic run usage exactly once, while fallback/downgrade candidates remain trace or journal events rather than a competing usage counter; verified by the child usage and trace contracts.
- [ ] The bespoke structured-output retry loop is removed only after the compatibility suite and authorized Anthropic/Bedrock cache canaries pass; verified by the cutover child source census, focused suite, and recorded live evidence.

## Child Decomposition
- The output-policy child adapts deterministic Rebar validation to Pydantic output processing and owns the first two policy-level acceptance outcomes.
- The bounded-operation child owns retry scheduling, request limits, complete-or-omit wire history, output-size guidance, and terminal refusal behavior.
- The compatibility child owns aggregate usage, narrow causal error restoration, diagnostics, and final-failure artifacts.
- The observability child owns candidate-identified fallback/downgrade traces without changing Pydantic usage semantics.
- The cutover child migrates remaining consumers, runs full and live parity evidence, and removes the obsolete retry path after its prerequisites land.

The children have non-overlapping policy ownership. Their explicit dependency edges enforce the expand-contract order.
